title: Alia Bhatt's Best Friend Married the Man Who Made Gunjan Saxena. Bollywood Showed Up.
excerpt: Akanksha Ranjan Kapoor and filmmaker Sharan Sharma tied the knot on the anniversary of their first date. The sangeet went viral. The reception was packed with stars.
body:
She proposed her own swayamvar. He played Jack Johnson while she was having an allergy attack. They got married on the exact anniversary of their first date, at her mother's home in Mumbai, in a ceremony so intimate it was over before most of the industry even knew it was happening.

**Akanksha Ranjan Kapoor** and filmmaker **Sharan Sharma** are officially married.

The couple tied the knot on July 11, 2026, in a registered ceremony at the Ranjan residence in Mumbai. It was, by Bollywood standards, almost aggressively low-key — no destination, no five-day spectacle, no paparazzi-managed exits. Just the couple, their families, and the legal paperwork. Akanksha wore a vibrant red saree with intricate gold zari work and heavy kundan jewellery. Sharan complemented her in a classic white kurta-pyjama with an embroidered jacket. In the photos she shared, they're either laughing, holding hands, or — in one particularly devastating image — she's crying as she signs the papers.

Her caption said everything:

> "Tu na toh ghar ghar nahi lagta, tu hai toh darr nahi lagta."
> (Without you, a house doesn't feel like home. When you're with me, I'm not afraid.)

## The Love Story Behind It

Akanksha and Sharan met through a mutual friend who showed her his Instagram profile with the unsolicited endorsement: "He thinks you're really cute. He really likes you." Her response was pure Bollywood-adjacent nonchalance: "That director dude? I've heard of him." She followed him back.

They later met at a birthday party that their friends jokingly called Akanksha's *swayamvar*. When asked who the girl he liked was, Sharan pointed her way. She thought they were becoming close friends. He corrected her: "There's a misconception there. I thought we were well beyond friends."

The proposal came during what Akanksha thought was a birthday trip to Alibaug. She wanted a bigger celebration; he wanted a private moment. So while she was dealing with an allergy attack and asking him to turn off the lights, he played **Jack Johnson's "Angel"** and got on one knee. She said yes, presumably between sneezes.

July 11 isn't a random date — it's the anniversary of their very first date four years ago.

## The Sangeet That Broke the Internet

If the wedding was intimate, the pre-wedding celebrations were anything but. The sangeet, held in Mumbai days before the ceremony, turned into the kind of evening that generates its own gravitational pull.

**Alia Bhatt** — Akanksha's childhood best friend and the reason half of Bollywood knows her name — showed up in a stunning purple saree and absolutely owned the dance floor with a performance to **Shah Rukh Khan's "Maahi Ve"** that immediately went viral. This wasn't a casual sway. This was full choreography, full commitment, full main-character energy from someone who technically wasn't the bride.

**Janhvi Kapoor** took on **"Shava Shava"** from *Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham*, and **Karan Johar** — because of course — recreated **Salman Khan's** infamous towel dance. The video clips circulated across every social media platform within hours.

## The Reception

The couple hosted a grand reception on July 12 at a Mumbai venue, and this time the industry came out in full force. **Sonakshi Sinha**, **Bobby Deol**, **Randeep Hooda**, and a constellation of Bollywood faces showed up to celebrate.

Alia Bhatt's mother, **Soni Razdan**, left what might be the most perfectly on-brand comment on Instagram: "Omg. Can't believe it… our baby got hitched and married to boot. Congratulations all round."

Social media personality **Orry** dropped his own wedding reel from the reception featuring **Janhvi Kapoor**, **Neeta Ambani**, and **Anant Ambani** — a guest list so eclectic that fans spent the day asking: "Whose wedding was this?"

## Who They Are

Akanksha's filmography includes Netflix's *Guilty* (2020), the recent courtroom thriller *Ikka* alongside **Sunny Deol** and **Akshaye Khanna**, and TVF's *Gram Chikitsalay* Season 2. She's not a headline star — not yet — but she's built a steady, respectable career in the streaming era.

Sharan Sharma, meanwhile, directed two of the more quietly significant Hindi films of recent years: *Gunjan Saxena: The Kargil Girl* (2020), which launched **Janhvi Kapoor** as a serious actor, and *Mr. & Mrs. Mahi* (2024), starring **Rajkummar Rao** and Janhvi again. He's the rare Bollywood filmmaker who's better known for the quality of his work than the noise around it.

Together, they're the kind of couple the industry doesn't always celebrate loudly enough — two people who've built their careers with craft rather than spectacle, who chose a registered ceremony over a three-continent wedding, and who managed to make even the allergy-attack proposal romantic.

## For the Diaspora

Both *Ikka* and *Gunjan Saxena* are available on **Netflix** globally, so there's no excuse not to catch up on the newlyweds' work. *Gram Chikitsalay* Season 2 is streaming on **TVF Play**. And Alia Bhatt's next project, *Love & War* with **Sanjay Leela Bhansali**, co-starring **Ranbir Kapoor** and **Vicky Kaushal**, is set for next year — a reminder that the circles these women run in are about to get even more interesting.

Congratulations to the Sharma-Ranjans. May the allergies stay manageable and the Jack Johnson never stop.
